To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SED-SL model is a new, simple but effective model that can be readily used to describe the transitional flows of flat plates and other geometries, with the correlation for transition location, Rex* = 1.2 × 106(0.7 + (Tu/2)−2)−1/2, and the transition Reynolds number, Rex* ≃ 3.3×106, being universal for all flat plate flows.

a two-state correlation of the stress length (SL), which is a key parameter in the SED theory, provides a simple yet accurate description of the transition process, and the resulting algebraic model predicts correctly for the entire streamwise friction coefficient profiles of all experimental and simulation data of flat plate turbulent boundary layers, with varying incoming turbulent intensity.

(i) the multi-layer stress length ℓ12 is a universal quantity in transitional flow; (ii) the SED-SL model is an accurate algebraic closure for transitional flows, and (iii) the SED theory is a powerful tool to study wall turbulence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the laminar-to-turbulent transition in a flat plate boundary layer, a fundamental problem of fluid dynamics.

the development of a novel, simple, and accurate description of laminar-to-turbulent transition of flat plate boundary layer flow based on the recently proposed structural ensemble dynamics (or SED) theory of wall-bounded turbulence.

the development of an accurate, simple, and general algebraic description of transitional flows, based on a structural theory of wall turbulence, which can be extended to engineering flows of practical interests, such as boundary-layer control, and drag reduction, etc.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present theory and the associated closure model are capable of providing a simple but accurate and robust description of transitional flows, with a universal correlation for the transition Reynolds number Rex* and a two-state structure for the multi-layer stress length function ℓ12.
the SED-SL model is a simple but accurate model for laminar-turbulence transition of flat plate boundary layer flows.
SED-SL is the first closure model that can accurately describe the laminar-turubulent transition of a flat plate boundary layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SED-SL model is able to describe accurately the entire streamwise evolution of transitional flows of flat plates, with the first ever two-state correlation for the transition location.

we have developed the SED-SL model to predict the entire streamwise evolution of Cf(x) of all seven sets (of experiments and simulation) of flat plate transitional data, with a correlation for transition location, Rex*, which is superior to other closures, and the model is extended to the prediction of transitional flow in the presence of pressure gradients.

a simple algebraic closure of SED theory, with only two parameters, can predict correctly the entire streamwise distributions of Cf(x) of transitional flows, for the first time, for all the available experimental and simulation data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the laminar-turingulent transition is characterized by a two-state structure of the stress length, which is the basis for the development of a new closure model for transitional flows.
the SED-SL model provides the first accurate algebraic description of the entire transitional flow of the flat plate boundary layer, which is a significant advance over the current state-of-art.
a two-state correlation of the SL function ℓ12, which is an essential component of the SED theory, is the key to understanding the laminar-tubulent transition.
